title: Loop Control Flags
pattern: A mutable boolean flag declared outside a loop, evaluated in the loop header, and modified inside the loop body solely to terminate execution on subsequent passes.
why_bad: Introduces dummy/unnecessary state. The reader is forced to trace all potential mutations of the flag throughout the entire loop block to understand loop termination.
detection: A mutable boolean variable evaluated in a loop condition and assigned a literal value inside the loop body to exit.
counterexample: A state variable that contains actual program data needed by code executing after the loop terminates.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring*, "Remove Control Flag"; Trevor Foucher & Dustin Boswell, *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 9.
